evidence: src/infrastructure/http/middleware/errorHandler.ts: `function statusFor(error: unknown): number` is the only place errors are mapped to HTTP status codes (400/404/409/500)
src/infrastructure/http/middleware/errorHandler.ts: `export const errorHandler: ErrorRequestHandler` writes `{ error: message }` or `{ error: 'Internal server error' }`

src/infrastructure/http/middleware/notFoundHandler.ts: `export const notFoundHandler: RequestHandler` writes `{ error: `Route ${req.method} ${req.path} not found` }` with status 404 for routes that do not match
Both files are imported only by src/infrastructure/http/app.ts as terminal middleware, which fits a single concern: HTTP error responses

Minor: the JSON error body shape { error: string } is written inline in both files instead of coming from a shared helper; this is a small risk of the shapes drifting apart, not a duplicated invariant
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files in the module do the same job: they are terminal Express middleware that turn unhandled outcomes into JSON HTTP error responses. errorHandler.ts maps thrown errors (domain ValidationError, NotFoundError and ConflictError, plus the HTTP-layer RequestValidationError and express.json SyntaxError) to status codes in one function, statusFor. notFoundHandler.ts handles requests that match no route. Both use the same Express handler types (ErrorRequestHandler and RequestHandler) and are wired up the same way from app.ts. The error-to-status mapping lives in one place and is not repeated. Both files return 404, but for different reasons: a domain entity that was not found versus a route that does not exist, so this is not a duplicated rule. The response body shape { error: string } is written inline three times, twice in errorHandler and once in notFoundHandler. That is a small risk of the shapes drifting apart, but it is not a real duplication of a business rule or a bypass of a shared abstraction, because the module has no shared response helper to bypass. Nothing in the module covers an unrelated concern.
